Title: Replying to a specific comment in a forum thread
Description: Steps to navigate from the forums index to a specific comment and submit a reply
- Start from the forums index page (URL containing '/forums') and click a specific forum link (e.g., 'AskReddit') to open the forum listing.
- On the forum listing page, locate the target post and click its 'comments' link (e.g., '16 comments') to open the comment thread.
- Identify the first reply in the thread and click the 'Reply' link associated with that specific comment.
- In the opened reply form, locate the 'Comment' textbox (often described with 'reply_to_comment_...').
- Fill the 'Comment' textbox with the required text (e.g., 'don't panic').
- Click the 'Post' button in the reply form to submit the comment.
- Verify the new comment appears in the thread after submission.

Title: Navigating forum replies and form submission
Description: Key UI signals and potential pitfalls when interacting with forum comment threads
- The 'Reply' link is attached to individual comments, not the main post; ensure you click the link under the specific comment you intend to answer.
- When replying to a comment, the form appears inline on the same page as the thread, not on a new page.
- The 'Comment' textbox in a reply form may be marked as 'required' and described by an attribute containing 'reply_to_comment_...'.
- If the initial URL returns a 404, navigate to the home page or forums index first to locate the correct post.
- Use 'go_back' and 'go_forward' cautiously; the home page may not display the post directly, requiring navigation via forums.
- The 'Post' button in the reply form is distinct from the main 'Post' button for creating new threads.
- After clicking 'Post', the page may reload or update in place, and the new comment should be visible immediately.
